Passages:
[1] [Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave > Eligibility, Entitlement and Planning Your Leave > Returning to Work at 50% Capacity]
Returning to work after parental leave can be challenging as you balance new family responsibilities while reintegrating into a workplace that has evolved during your absence.

To support this transition, GitLab offers team members the option to return at 50% capacity. This program is not tracked in Workday and does not require the Absence Management team’s review or approval. To utilize this benefit:

- Discuss with your manager before starting leave or a few weeks prior to returning
- Work together to determine a schedule that works for both you and your team
- The standard guideline is two to four weeks at reduced capacity, though this can be adjusted based on individual needs
- The 50% figure is flexible, and doesn’t always have to equate to working hours. Some options to consider would be:
  - Adjusting the workload so you’re slowly ramping back up to a full plate - this won’t look the same for everyone - some team members may prefer to ramp up more quickly
  - Adjust the working days/hours so instead of working 5-8hrs days it could be 4-10hrs, or you work really early in the morning/late in the evening
  - Slowly increase the number of working days each week (i.e. 2 days the first week, 3 days the second, etc.)

This transition period gives you space to adjust to your new normal without the pressure of a full workload, allowing time to resolve any unexpected childcare challenges or other family adjustments.

[2] [Leave of Absence Toolkit for Team Members and Managers > Team Member Toolkit > Pre-Leave]
We recognize that the nature of the leave will impact the amount of notice a team member may be able to provide (i.e. more planning and advanced notice will be given for parental leaves vs. a medical leave which could arise unexpectedly). When possible, team members should:

- Prepare a coverage plan with their managers and fellow team members.
- Set an out of office message in Gmail and identify someone to contact during their absence. Slack and Gcal will also need to be updated to reflect the absence.
- Parental Leave:
  - Consider support from [Parentaly](https://www.parentaly.com/join/coaching-program/gitlab) to help you build a strong coverage plan, transition your work effectively and return to work with confidence after leave. You can read more about this benefit and how to sign-up in the [Parental Leave Support (Parentaly)](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave-support-parentaly) handbook section.
  - Watch the videos below from Parentaly:
  - [Creating a strong career vision through parental leave](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HlmubbY64QU)
  - [When to start the coverage planning process](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dpdh-QLlz_4)
  - [Why it’s hard for employees to return to work after parental leave](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h8vLKiMPBV8)

[3] [Leave Types > GitLab Parental Leave > Eligibility, Entitlement and Planning Your Leave > Returning to Work]
It’s important to acknowledge that returning to work after Parental Leave can be difficult. Even with smooth reentries, life and work interplay differently when one adds another member to their family. Everyone transitions differently, and the impact on an individual varies depending on role, as well as a litany of personal factors.

About a week before your expected return, the Absence Management team will send you a welcome back email which will share resources and ask you to confirm your return to work date. **Please respond by confirming the date you will return.**

More Return-to-work Resources shared [here](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave).

Question: What steps should a GitLab employee take to arrange a 50% capacity return after parental leave?

Answer:
Based on the provided context, a GitLab employee should take the following steps to arrange a 50% capacity return after parental leave:

1.  **Discuss with their manager:** This conversation should happen either before starting the leave or a few weeks prior to returning.
2.  **Collaborate on a schedule:** Work together with the manager to determine a schedule that works for both the employee and the team.
3.  **Define the reduced capacity:** While the standard guideline is two to four weeks, the specific arrangement can be adjusted based on individual needs. The "50%" figure is flexible and can be implemented in various ways, such as:
    *   Adjusting the workload to slowly ramp up to a full plate.
    *   Adjusting working days or hours (e.g., working 4–10 hours instead of 5–8, or shifting to early morning/late evening hours).
    *   Gradually increasing the number of working days per week (e.g., 2 days the first week, 3 days the second, etc.).

Note that this program does not require review or approval from the Absence Management team and is not tracked in Workday.
